What the analyzer showed us — and what the guide says it means

Step 1: the error message
Messages screen on site — 24/05/02 11:08, severity Error

Reading the error code

033

Incubator 2 — Transition

Heater

Problem with the chip that powers the heater or the fan

One code, five possible parts. The small number in brackets picks which one — next slide.

Panther | Case Study – Transition Incubator (Inc. 2)
“(error 2)” means the side heater
From the Panther troubleshooting guide

For error 00116, the number in brackets tells you which part has the problem:

Error #PartWhat the guide says to do
0Bottom heater 1Check bottom heater / replace incubator
1Bottom heater 2Check bottom heater / replace incubator
2Side (wall) heater 1Check side heater / replace incubator
3Side (wall) heater 2Check side heater / replace incubator
4FanCheck fan / replace fan

What this told us

  • “Wall heater” is the side heater, plugged into J10 “Heat Bottom”
  • The fan is off the list — it would be error 4
  • In the guide's example, this error came from the heater, not the board
  • So: test the heater first, not the board

From the Panther troubleshooting guide

With a side heater problem, the incubator starts up but never locks — it stops about 1–2 °C short.

43.7 − 1.0 = 42.7

Target minus one degree gives our reading almost exactly. Power and control work — one heater just isn't doing its part.

The steps we followed
1

Read the message

033.001.00116 (error 2) → side heater

2

Check temperatures

Inc. 2 at 42.70 °C — 1 °C below target, never locks

3

Check other causes

Room temp OK, other incubators OK, not a fan error

4

Open the Mid Bay

Remove the Mid Bay cover, check plugs J9, J10, J14, J15

5

Measure the heaters

Switch off, unplug, Tests A, B, C on each heater

6

Fix it

Side heater broken → fit a good one from an old Transition incubator

From the troubleshooting guide

Bottom heater on the left plug, side heater on the right. On our unit all plugs were correct and tight — so we went on to measure the heaters.

The side heater: a flat heater on the incubator wall. Its orange (+) and blue (−) wires run to the J10 plug.

Bottom heater (J9): reading too low = bad — often shows as a chip error

Side heater (J10): reading too high or open = bad — starts up but never locks

Root cause & fix

A broken side heater — and how we fixed it without a new incubator

Root cause: broken side heater
1

Side heater breaks

No current flows → error 2

2

Less heat

Bottom heater still works; incubator starts up

3

Stuck at ~42.7 °C

Can't reach the last degree

4

Never locks

Below 43.2 °C → red, can't run tests

What proved it

  • Error 2 = side (wall) heater 1
  • Inc. 2 exactly 1.0 °C below target — just like the guide says
  • Room temp, Inc. 1 and Inc. 3 normal — the rest of the analyzer is fine
  • All heater plugs correct and tight
  • Side heater reads open instead of 12–16 Ω
Panther | Case Study – Transition Incubator (Inc. 2)
The fix: a side heater from an old incubator

The guide says: replace the whole incubator

The guide says the heater can't be replaced on its own — a broken heater means a new incubator.

Not what we did

What we did: replace only the side heater

We took an old, non-working Transition incubator, removed its good side heater, and fitted it in place of the broken one.

Our case — side heater replaced

Not in the manual: there are no steps for removing the side heater. The team worked out how to take it out and fit it themselves.

Incubator opened — side heater on its wall

Why a Transition unit

The three incubators are different and can't be swapped, so the heater had to come from the same type.

What it saved

A whole new incubator — the customer's unit kept its board, fan and carousel.

Guide: the three incubators are different — they can't be swapped
Panther | Case Study – Transition Incubator (Inc. 2)
Checks after the fix

What we checked

  1. Old unit's side heater measured with Tests A/B/C (12–16 Ω) before fitting
  2. J10 and J15 plugged back in, incubator closed
  3. Analyzer restarts with no error
  4. Temperatures reach target and lock (wait ~30 min)
  5. No new 033.001.00116 error
  6. Full system check (OQ) with no errors

What we learned

Read the error number

For error 00116: 0–1 = bottom heater, 2–3 = side heater, 4 = fan.

1 °C low and no lock = side heater

Incubator heats but never locks? Check the side heater first.

Old units can give good parts

An old, non-working Transition incubator gave us a good side heater — no new incubator.

Measure before changing parts

Tests A/B/C: about 14 Ω per heater — on the faulty unit and on the part you fit.
